scope: Catalogue segmentation, re-identification, count-version and inspection-depth changes in Hodgson manuscript collections, initialized from Rajendralal Mitra 1882 and related Hunter/Cowell-Eggeling catalogue states.

source_core.citation: Rajendralal Mitra, The Sanskrit Buddhist Literature of Nepal, Asiatic Society of Bengal, 1882

error_types.FALSE_SPLIT: one textual work represented under two or more names as separate works
error_types.FALSE_LUMP: two or more textual works represented under one name/entry
error_types.PHYSICAL_TEXTUAL_COLLAPSE: physical codex or volume boundary assumed to equal textual-work boundary
error_types.BOUNDARY_SAMPLING_ERROR: inspection of first/last page or other limited boundary sample misses internal work transitions
error_types.UNDERDESCRIBED_COMPOSITE: composite identity recognized but internal contents represented too coarsely for the later analytical task
error_types.RESEGMENTED_COMPOSITE: stable physical/institutional unit receives a finer enumeration of internal textual units after deeper inspection
error_types.LATER_REIDENTIFICATION: identity corrected through deeper inspection or comparison with other witnesses/lists
error_types.CATALOGUE_VERSION_OBSOLESCENCE: printed or institutional catalogue preserves an earlier known-imperfect descriptive state
error_types.COUNT_VERSION_CONFLICT: same or apparently overlapping collection receives non-identical count states whose conversion genealogy is unresolved

records.collection: Hodgson Sanskrit Buddhist manuscripts / Calcutta collection
records.historical_actor_diagnosis: Mitra states the preserved list sometimes described the same work under two or three names as different works.
records.physical_cause: not individually specified for false-split cases
records.article_value: Catalogue error can change cardinality without material loss or acquisition.

records.collection: Hodgson Sanskrit Buddhist manuscripts / Calcutta collection
records.historical_actor_diagnosis: Mitra states one name was sometimes given to four, five, or more different works.
records.physical_cause: multiple different works written continuously in a single physical volume without a break in pagination
records.inspection_protocol: cursory examination reading only first and last page of each codex to determine volume name
records.article_value: Direct material mechanism for false object segmentation.

records.collection: Hodgson Sanskrit Buddhist manuscripts / Calcutta collection
records.historical_actor_diagnosis: Distinct textual works could share one continuously paginated volume.
records.physical_cause: bound/assembled codex unity plus uninterrupted pagination
records.inspection_protocol: physical-volume boundary treated as proxy for textual-work boundary
records.effect_on_count: physical volume and textual work become falsely equated

records.collection: Hodgson Sanskrit Buddhist manuscripts / Calcutta collection
records.historical_actor_diagnosis: Only first and last page of codex were read during cursory naming.
records.effect_on_count: internal works remain invisible as separate catalogue objects
records.article_value: Catalogue accuracy depends on sampling protocol, not only linguistic competence.

records.collection: Hodgson Sanskrit manuscripts distributed to multiple institutions
records.catalogue: W. W. Hunter, Catalogue of Sanskrit Manuscripts collected in Nepal and presented to various Libraries and Learned Societies by Brian Houghton Hodgson, 1881
records.provenance_of_calcutta_list: Mitra states he compiled it from records of the Asiatic Society office for Hunter

records.effect_on_count: printed catalogue fixes a known-imperfect intermediate identity state

records.catalogue: Rajendralal Mitra, The Sanskrit Buddhist Literature of Nepal
records.inspection_protocol: detailed manuscript analysis including material/codicological fields and textual contents
records.effect_on_count: supports finer segmentation and more stable identification
records.article_value: More intensive material inspection can change textual identity and catalogue cardinality.

records.catalogue: E. B. Cowell and J. Eggeling, Catalogue of Buddhist Sanskrit Manuscripts in the possession of the Royal Asiatic Society (Hodgson Collection)
records.stated_limit: detailed analysis may be difficult or impossible without comparison with other copies
records.inspection_protocol: brief identification-oriented description with explicit recognition of comparison requirements
records.article_value: Contemporary cataloguers explicitly calibrated description depth to identification task.

records.earlier_description: Dharani-mantra-sangraha, B.5, described earlier in Mitra at p.80
records.later_diagnosis: Mitra states the earlier description did not convey a full idea of B.5 contents and later enumerates 39 Dharanis.

overlap_relation.relation: Mitra states some B.65 Dharanis are included in B.5

records.effect_on_count: one stable institutional aggregate becomes representable as 39 internal textual units without requiring a new outer identifier
records.article_value: Inspection depth changes represented object granularity; legitimate composite and false lump must be distinguished.

count_versions.context: collection as immediate object of Mitra's analysis

records.warning: False splitting and false lumping both existed, and bundle count also changes; do not attribute the 26-work difference mechanically to false-lump correction.
records.article_value: A count is a versioned descriptive output, not timeless metadata.

count_conversion_evidence.warning: Do not generalize this ratio to Fort William or other shipments; it proves only that bundle and work counts are non-identical and can have many-to-many relations.
Do not silently merge with the 85/144 distribution statement; their genealogy remains unresolved.

catalogue_labour_observation.institutional_patronage: Arthur Grote repeatedly urged analysis; Asiatic Society Council accepted divided work and agreed to defray preparation/printing cost.
division_of_labour: Harinath Vidyaratna read about two-thirds of texts and prepared Sanskrit abstracts under Mitra
Ramanath Tarkaratna read the large Prajnaparamita
Kamakhyanath Tarkayagisa read three smaller works
Mitra read the remainder and frequently checked abstracts against originals
Haraprasad Sastri translated abstracts of 16 larger works into English
catalogue_labour_observation.verification_limit: Mitra states he did not compare all Haraprasad renderings with originals.
catalogue_labour_observation.scope_change: Difficulty with Buddhist philosophical terminology and condensation contributed to abandoning a broad doctrinal review in favour of narratives/stories.

testable_claims: Material codex unity could be mistaken for textual unity when inspection sampled only boundary pages.
Catalogue practices could alter the perceived number of works without any physical acquisition or loss.
Increasing inspection depth can change segmentation and therefore object identity or internal object count.
A stable institutional identifier can legitimately describe a composite whose internal textual units are later enumerated more finely.
Printed catalogues should be treated as versioned interventions in the identity history of collections.
Institutional legibility depended on funded and divided expert labour, intermediate abstracts, selective checking and editorial constraints.
